items: lies along the inferior liver surface; identify the fundus, body, and neck.
connects the gallbladder neck to the extrahepatic biliary tree; neck or duct obstruction can prevent drainage.
traverses liver before entering the gallbladder; assess intervening hepatic vessels.
enters the gallbladder without traversing liver; requires a safe window without intervening bowel.

transhepatic access carries greater bleeding risk but may help contain bile leakage. Transperitoneal access avoids liver traversal but has a theoretical greater bile-leak/biloma risk; comparative studies have not consistently shown a difference in leakage. Choose the safest patient-specific route.
map the colon, duodenum, pleura, and vessels along the planned trajectory.

Access needle: 18G Chiba/Seldinger needle with removable stylet; commonly 10-20 cm, chosen for depth. Confirm 0.035-inch wire compatibility.
Alternative access: AccuStick II - 21G needle, 0.018-inch wire, 4 Fr dilator/6 Fr sheath; then exchange to the working wire.
Working wire: 0.035-inch Amplatz, soft tip.
Drain: 8.5 or 10.2 Fr locking pigtail (MPD/Dawson-Mueller).
Dilator: matched to drain size; blunt metal catheter stiffener.
Imaging: ultrasound probe/sterile cover; fluoroscopy.
Local anesthetic: lidocaine, syringe, injection needle.
Sterile supplies: gloves, gown, skin prep, drapes, towels, gauze.
Scalpel: #11 blade.
Injection/sampling: saline, contrast, syringes, specimen container.
Securement: 2-0 nonabsorbable Prolene, needle driver, forceps/Kelly, scissors.
Drainage: gravity bag, connector/stopcock, dressing.

review CT/US for gallbladder distention, wall, bowel, liver, and pleura. Prefer a transhepatic route when safe: better anchoring and less bile leakage, but liver traversal adds bleeding risk. If coagulopathic, discuss correction and transperitoneal access; it avoids liver traversal but may leak/dislodge more readily.
confirm antibiotic coverage. Use sterile gloves/gown, skin prep, drapes, and towels. Visualize the gallbladder with ultrasound; infiltrate lidocaine along the tract and hepatic capsule.

advance the 18G Chiba/Seldinger needle under ultrasound, avoiding vessels and the far wall. Remove the needle stylet, aspirate bile, and collect ordered cultures. The outer needle cannula stays for wire passage; it is not the drain stiffener.

blocks.alt: Ultrasound showing a needle along a transhepatic course into the gallbladder lumen.
blocks.caption: Ultrasound: transhepatic needle access into the gallbladder.

items: pass a compatible 0.035-inch Amplatz through the cannula under fluoroscopy; coil its soft tip within the gallbladder. Stop for resistance or extra-luminal course. Remove the cannula while holding wire access.

flush an 8.5 or 10.2 Fr locking pigtail drain and insert its blunt metal stiffening cannula. Make a skin nick and dilate over the wire with the kit dilator for the chosen drain; avoid advancing beyond the measured lumen depth.

advance drain/stiffener over the wire under fluoroscopy. Once the rigid tip is inside the lumen, hold it stationary, loosen the hub, and advance the catheter off it. Do not tee off with the rigid tip still in the gallbladder wall; never advance a sharp trocar over the wire.

remove wire and stiffener. Gently pull the retention string to form the loop; confirm the loop and all sideholes lie in the gallbladder. Use a small gentle contrast injection to confirm position without overdistending an infected gallbladder.

blocks.alt: Fluoroscopic image of a pigtail drainage catheter within the gallbladder.
blocks.caption: Fluoroscopy: pigtail drain within the gallbladder.

items: use the actual hub mechanism: for Mac-Loc, hold the hub, tension the string, and close the cam lever until it clicks. Do not over-tighten the loop or assume every drain uses the same colored locking piece.

use 2-0 nonabsorbable Prolene with needle driver/forceps. Place a skin anchor without blanching. Local Roman-sandal technique: cross tails around the tube and tie 4/4/4/7 throws, noting attending/device preference. Keep the tube lumen round; do not puncture or cinch the tubing.
attach to gravity drainage, check free bile return, and dress the site. Save final imaging; document drain size, route, locking, and flush plan.

avoid forceful wire advancement and confirm all side holes are intraluminal.
assess new bloody output, worsening pain, or instability for vascular injury.

blocks.title: Routine orders
items: Diet - Outpatient: order regular diet. Inpatient: notify primary team diet is okay.
Vital signs per unit routine.
Tylenol 650 mg PRN.

blocks.title: Access care
items: Flush with 10 mL sterile saline once daily.

blocks.title: Anticoagulation to resume
items: Warfarin: 24 hours.
IV unfractionated heparin: 6-8 hours.
Enoxaparin: 12 hours.
DOACs: Typically 24 hours; confirm agent and renal function.
Clopidogrel: 75 mg dose - 6 hours; 300-600 mg loading dose - 24 hours.
Aspirin: 24 hours.
Restart after hemostasis is confirmed; individualize timing for procedure-specific or patient-specific exceptions.

blocks.title: Follow up
items: Surgery manages and tube comes out with cholecystectomy.
Drain check in 2-3 months.
